_comment: CI READ ROLE — the ONLY AWS permissions a Correlix release build holds.
A release READS corresponding source out of the archive and places it in the
bundle. It never writes, never deletes, never adjusts a retention date and
never bypasses one. That is not a convention in a script; it is the absence of
the permission. If publish-images.yml were compromised tomorrow, the archive
would still be intact, because this document grants nothing that could damage
DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and asserted absent by tests/test_source_archive.py:
s3:DeleteBucket, s3:PutBucketPolicy, and every non-S3 action.
ListBucket is scoped by prefix condition rather than granted bucket-wide: the
release needs to resolve keys under sources/, components/ and releases/, and
nothing else in the account's namespace.
${bucket_arn} is substituted by Terraform (templatefile). Tests read this file
as data and assert what it does NOT allow.

_why: Belt and braces. The Allow statements above already grant no write, but an
explicit Deny cannot be undone by a later Allow attached to the same role,
by a permissions boundary change, or by a resource policy. A read role that
can be silently promoted to a write role by an unrelated policy edit is not
